source.title: A Note on Generalization in Variational Autoencoders: How Effective Is Synthetic Data&Overparameterization?
source.authors: Tim Z. Xiao; Johannes Zenn; Robert Bamler

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps two distinct VAE parameter groups and reports that double descent appears when their sizes are combined along a chosen trajectory, while individual-axis sweeps show different shapes. It presents this as a refinement of the general double-descent account.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports results on synthetic data, augmentations, and other VAE performance gaps. The synthetic-data sample-count sweep is recorded under fits_no_version because it does not examine the interpolation-threshold condition in V3. Results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study sweeps two VAE width axes on CIFAR-10 and reports test-ELBO curves. Each single-axis sweep is U-shaped or L-shaped. A down-up-down curve appears only when a chosen sequence across both axes is plotted against total parameter count. The authors present this as consistent with Curth et al.'s artifact account. Their own results therefore bear on V1 (model-wise double descent in a deep network) and V7 (double descent as an artifact of how complexity is counted).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find that single-axis sweeps give U- or L-shaped test-ELBO curves. Double-descent 'indications' appear only when parameters are increased sequentially along two axes and plotted against total parameter count. They link this to Curth et al.'s account for non-deep models and defer a detailed investigation to future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses VAE test ELBO and negative test ELBO while varying latent-dimension and internal-channel parameters, rather than reproducing the original model-size/error experiments. It also combines two parameter axes along a selected trajectory.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed shape depends on which parameter group is increased and on the chosen sequence for increasing the two groups.

fits_no_version.finding: Test ELBO rises with synthetic diffusion-model sample count k and plateaus for k ≥ 10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the CIFAR-10 VAE, about 10×|Dtrain| diffusion samples give generalization similar to 1000×.

record.problems: The size-sweep findings are mainly shown in figures without numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The study does not identify an interpolation threshold, and the reported combined double-descent trajectory is explicitly chosen to produce that shape.
record.rows_left_out: No additional size-sweep rows left out. Other reported performance metrics and synthetic-data comparisons do not directly measure the versions tested here.

untested.parts: No interpolation threshold is located, so it is untested whether any peak sits near the size that just fits the training set.
Epoch curves (Fig. 2, 5, 14) show classical overfitting, but no epoch-wise double-descent analysis is made.
No sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
Only VAEs (deep networks) are tested; no other model classes and no interpolation point.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location.
No tests of label noise, multiple peaks, or tuned regularization.
No effective parameter measure is computed. The study only separates raw parameter counts per axis and does not show that the second descent becomes a U-shape under such a measure.

record.verdict_notes: The record omitted V7. The paper's double-descent section is effectively a demonstration of the Curth et al. artifact argument in a deep VAE, so V7 is added. V4 links are dropped because only deep networks are tested. The duplicate supports/limits_scope labels on R6 for V1 are merged into limits_scope, since the shape depends on the authors' choice of trajectory. All size-sweep evidence is figure-only, with no numeric values or uncertainty. Several rows carry different states for V1 and V7, which the problem field explains.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not locate a training-set interpolation threshold or test whether a peak occurs near it.
The paper plots training progress and discusses overfitting, but does not test fall-rise-fall test error over epochs.
No sample-size increase near an interpolation threshold is tested.
The study does not identify an interpolation point, and tests only VAE parameter sweeps rather than a range of model classes.
The study discusses distinct parameter axes but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations.
The study does not test noise-driven peaks, multiple descent peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
The study does not measure performance against an appropriate effective parameter count to establish that the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shape.

rows.value: figure only; text states test ELBO increases through mz = 16 and then stays around the same level
rows.note: The reported trend does not show the fall-rise-fall risk pattern; ELBO improves and then plateaus.

conditions.value: mz = 1 with nc increased to 256; then nc = 256 with mz increased to 64; then mz = 64 with nc increased to 512

rows.value: figure only; text describes the negative test ELBO as going down, up, and down again
rows.note: The authors say the double-descent appearance is artificially enforced by the chosen trajectory through the two parameter axes.
rows.check: A down-up-down curve appears only along a trajectory the authors chose, and they call it artificially enforced. For V1 it should count as dependent on that construction, not as a natural peak; no interpolation threshold is located. For V7 it is observed: the double descent arises from plotting against aggregate parameter count. The study does not state training length for these runs; 1000 epochs (the setup default) is likely.
